findings.statement: Burp refuses a hotkey when EITHER side is taken: burp.Zfhv.ZT(III)V asserts `this.Z_.get(chord) == null` (no other action on that chord) and `this.Zp.get(actionId) == null` (that action has no chord) before it writes the two maps. A rebuild must reject both directions, not just the chord.

The hotkey settings file is authoritative, not an overlay: burp.Zfhv.Zh(Z_dk) reads it, maps the stored entries, drops later duplicates by keystroke (HashSet of ZI()), then applies them through Z_(), which first clears the whole registry via ZL(). So an action absent from the file ends up with no hotkey at all.

Class and method names can be made readable without any craft/REA rename tool: JarRemapper rewrites the jar's bytecode from a class map plus a method map, and the remapped jar then loads and runs (SuiteCommand.label()/id()/category()/commandId() verified by reflection), so craft's decompiler shows `HotkeyRegistry.applyBinding` instead of `Zfhv.ZT`. Mapping rules are in re/mapping/README.md.

Burp's CA certificate is fetched through the proxy, not from disk: the browser must already be proxying through the listener, then visits http://burpsuite, which Burp itself answers. WebProbe reproduces that with http://webprobe (and the Burp host) answered locally by the proxy, serving the CA as PEM and DER.

Burp verifies a working CA install by visiting any HTTPS URL and confirming there is no security warning, and notes that most users never install it because the bundled browser is preconfigured. WebProbe has no bundled browser (task L-05), so its checklist verifies by counting decrypted HTTPS exchanges in history and says so.

An unset attribute reads 0 (Zeua.Za). burp.Zr2x per-side retain rules, burp.Zsnr comparator (CC/SSN/email/JSON-node counts excluded), and burp.Zmaq driver: rounds 4/6/10 read from Burp's own Zmaq.ZA at runtime, NORMAL = 6 = the AuditDefaults scan_accuracy default; the baseline seeds the positive side; true/false sides alternate. Payloads are '<prefix>)(' + objectClass=* under k%6 negations (even = always true, odd = never true). The random 10-char prefix is tried first at NORMAL speed, then '*'. Payloads replace the value. Wave 34: boolean SQL injection ported from Burp's SQL engine burp.Zppj (behind SqlAndXPathInjectionCheck burp.Zg_c -> Zw7s). Payload generators burp.Zguq: Zguz '<r>{q} or {q}{n}{q}={q}{v}', Zgut '<r>{q} or {n}={v}-- ', Zgua '{q} and {q}{n}{q}={q}{v}', Zgu3 '{q} and {n}={v}-- '. The ' or '/' and ' literals were decoded at runtime. r is in [10^7,10^8). Positive: n in [1000,10000) vs itself; when unquoted, every 4th (starting with the first) vs '0n'. Negative: m in [1009,9990) vs m+k, k in [1,10); every 4th (2nd, 6th, ...) vs m+quote or m+'0'. Order follows Zppj.Zi/ZL: unquoted (gated on Zgx0.ZO/Zs, which is not decompilable; WebProbe uses 'numeric value' for it, inferred), then quote ', each OR, OR-comment, and at NORMAL also AND and AND-comment. Then the numeric pairs Zppj.Zh replace the value, cycled by Zht3: ['(select abs(1))','(select 1)','1','000001'] vs ['(select sba(1))','(seletc 1)','0','100000']. String pairs are appended to the value (Zx4k mode 1). Every attempt runs through the ported Zmaq differential engine with the base response. This replaces WebProbe's invented AND 1=1/AND 1=2 length-threshold probe. Test sink models the original query's closing quote; Burp's every-4th quoted negative becomes a syntax error, as in a real database. Suite 259 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored. Still open in Zppj: error-based (ZE, signatures encrypted), time-based (ZT), and the backslash-powered differences step.
